title: Port of Baltimore closure after the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, March-June 2024
why_this_event: BENCHMARK #2, chosen to test whether the Yantian failure pattern is a property of the MODEL or of the Yantian proxy. It differs from Yantian on every dimension that could have caused a spurious result: different year (2024 vs 2021), different continent, different trigger (physical channel blockage vs COVID labour absence), and critically OUTSIDE the 2021 global congestion wave that confounded the Yantian observations.
The capacity loss is near-total and unambiguous — the navigation channel was physically blocked — so the injected shock needs no estimation of an operating percentage.
The restoration timeline is documented to the day by a public academic reference source, which gives DATED MILESTONES even though no weekly throughput series exists.
Duration (~11 weeks to full channel reopening) is long enough to resolve recovery dynamics at weekly resolution, and is about twice Yantian's, so a 'recovery too fast' error should be easier to see.
Chosen despite a known weakness: the disrupted port's own monthly throughput could not be obtained publicly. That weakness is itself part of the finding.

port_capacity.note: Baseline by construction: the index is defined so that normal pre-event operation is 100. Not an observation. No other variable is initialised from data, because no admissible pre-cutoff series for this port was obtainable — so the model runs on module defaults downstream, and that is stated rather than hidden.

event.label: Federal navigation channel blocked; container throughput to zero
event.description: At about 01:30 on 26 March 2024 the containership MV Dali lost steering and struck a support pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, collapsing it across the Fort McHenry federal navigation channel and closing the Port of Baltimore's main terminals to deep-draught container traffic.

evidence.note: Channel blocked by the collapsed span; container access to the main terminals cut.

event_status_note: DESIGN DECISION, and the point of this replay: only the INITIATING shock is injected, for a single week. The phased channel restoration is deliberately NOT injected. Everything after week 1 — including the entire recovery path of port_capacity — is a pure model OUTPUT, so the observed restoration milestones are a genuine falsification test of the model's recovery dynamics rather than a check on an input we supplied. This is the opposite of the Yantian setup, where the capacity path was injected in phases and therefore untestable.
description: Weekly replay of the 2024 Baltimore port closure. Week 1 begins 2024-03-26. A single one-week shock takes port_capacity to zero; the model must then recover on its own. Evaluation is by DATED MILESTONES rather than a level series, because no weekly or monthly throughput series for the port was publicly obtainable.
